s1.text: 07:10 — You walk to bed 12 to check Mr. Somchai’s blood pressure. What do you do first?

choices.text: Clean my hands with alcohol rub at the bedside
choices.feedback: Correct — moment 1, before touching the patient.
Gloves are not needed for blood pressure — and gloves never replace moment 1.

s1b.text: You put on gloves without cleaning your hands. Germs from the corridor are now inside the gloves and on the cuff.

s2.text: 07:15 — The IV line needs a new dressing. Your hands are clean from moment 1, but you touched the bed rail since then. What now?

choices.text: Clean hands again before the dressing
choices.feedback: Correct — moment 2, right before an aseptic task.

choices.text: Go ahead — I already cleaned them
choices.feedback: The bed rail re-contaminated your hands.

s2b.text: Touching the rail moved germs back onto your hands, and now onto the IV site. This is how line infections start.

s3.text: 07:25 — Done. You straightened the bed sheet on your way out but did not touch Mr. Somchai. Next is bed 13.

choices.text: Clean my hands before going to bed 13
choices.feedback: Correct — moment 5, after touching patient surroundings.

choices.text: Go straight to bed 13 — I did not touch the patient
choices.feedback: The sheet is inside the patient zone.

s3b.text: You carried germs from bed 12’s sheet to bed 13. Moment 5 is the most forgotten moment.

end.text: Well done — you used moments 1, 2 and 5 correctly on one short round.
